brief: US equities are seeing a partial tech-led rebound from Thursday's historic selloff, in which the NDX lost a record $2.3tn in market value in a single day. The recovery is driven by improved sentiment after Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa signaled existing AI data-center construction can proceed while AI-related legislation is finalized, though the rebound is losing steam after reports Microsoft is scaling back AI cloud capacity rented from Oracle, and the NDX has pared an intraday gain of over 2% to +1.2%. Beneath the headline recovery, breadth is weak (over 60% of SPX constituents lower), and Citi's cash desk shows inflows into Financials/Consumer Discretionary against outflows from Info Tech, Industrials, Comm Services, Healthcare, Energy and Staples, so the desk reads the tape as unconvinced rather than resolved. Separately, October payrolls more than doubled expectations (+165k), pushing front-end UST yields modestly higher, a hawkish counterweight to the tech dip-buying bid. In FX, the dollar is firm but off its highs; CAD and AUD underperform on soft data, and eFX flow is selling NZD/CAD/CHF against NOK/MXN buying. Citi's economists expect Tuesday's core and headline CPI to print below consensus, at 0.19% and 0.16% MoM respectively.
